title: presets
description: The providers and models Neuman supports, as the server ships them (D76). An operator adds a provider from a preset by supplying a key, and a model by choosing it on a provider they have; the server builds the baseline entry from the preset and refuses a later edit that contradicts one of its facts. Facts are what the model or the route *is* -- the window, whether it can see, the reasoning dialect and the levels a route forwards, the provider's id -- and belong to the release. Policy is what the operator may change: reply length, prices, the default reasoning level. A model reached on this machine's GPU is a `local` route beside the hosted ones: its facts are the weights pinned to a Hugging Face commit and the flags the model needs, and its policy is what the machine chooses. Assembled by the server from one file per entry under `neuman_server/presets/`, keyed by the file's stem.

logo.description: A file stem under the client's `logos/` directory. The client draws a monogram when the file is absent.

notes.description: One or two sentences an operator reads before choosing: what this is for, and what it trades.

url.description: The OpenAI-compatible base URL; `/chat/completions` is appended. https only: a preset is a hosted provider, and the key crosses on every request.

key_url.description: Where an operator creates a key for this provider.

name.description: The catalog name the model is added under unless the operator chooses another: the string a user picks in the composer and a role's `models` grant names.

routes.description: Provider preset id -> what is true of this model reached there. A model reached through two providers shares its window and nothing else: the id, the output ceiling, the prices and which reasoning levels are forwarded all belong to the route. Absent for a model offered only on this machine.

verified.description: When and from what the route's facts were read, e.g. `2026-10-16, GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models`. A fact without a source is a guess.

dialect.description: The reasoning dialect and the levels this route accepts: baseline.schema.json#/$defs/reasoning without the default, which is policy.

policy.description: Starting values the operator may change after adding the model. A route's policy is merged over the model's.

reasoning_default.description: Must be one of the route's reasoning levels; the server checks this when it loads the presets.

localRoute.description: The model run on this machine's GPU. Separate from `routes` because nothing here is a provider's: the weights are fetched from Hugging Face into `modelsDir`, and the runtime is started with the flags below.

name.description: The catalog name the local model is added under, when it must differ from the model's own: the same weights hosted elsewhere are a second entry, and two entries cannot share the name a user picks.

verified.description: When and from what the facts were read: the Hub API for the pin, a run on named hardware for `vram`.

model_flags.description: Flags the model needs on any hardware, such as `--jinja`, without which llama.cpp uses a generic chat template and the model's tool calls do not parse. Flags that are the machine's choice are policy fields, never these.

weights.description: What to download, pinned. A revision rather than a branch, and a hash per file, so the bytes a release was measured against are the bytes every appliance runs.

name.description: The file's name under `modelsDir`, and in the repository unless `path` says otherwise. No directories: a name that could leave `modelsDir` is refused by the schema rather than by every reader.

path.description: Where the file is in the repository when that is not `name` at its root, as for a quantisation published under a directory of its own. Only the download reads it: the file is saved as `name`, so every shard of a split model sits beside the first, where llama.cpp looks for them.

role.description: `model` is the weights: one file, or every shard of a split GGUF in order (`-00001-of-0000N.gguf` first), of which the runtime is started with the first and finds the rest beside it. `mmproj` is the vision projector. A model sees exactly when it has one.

vram.description: What the runtime held on the GPU at the route's default policy. Measured, not computed: it depends on the window, the cache type, the projector and speculation as much as on the file. A proposal for whether the model fits, never a refusal.

measured.description: Where and how, e.g. `2026-11-02, RTX 3090, nvidia-smi per-process`.

localPolicy.description: Starting values the operator may change. Typed fields, not a command line: the runtime builds its own argv from these, so a stored document can never hand it an arbitrary flag or file.

context_size.description: The window the runtime is started with (`--ctx-size`). A VRAM decision, not a fact about the model.

gpu_layers.description: Layers offloaded to the GPU; 99 is all of any model shipped here.

speculation.description: Speculative decoding against the model's own multi-token-prediction head. Policy because the draft context costs VRAM the window could have.

kv_cache.description: The number format of the attention cache, both K and V (`--cache-type-k`, `--cache-type-v`). Absent is `f16`, llama.cpp's own. `q8_0` holds the cache in about half the memory, so the same card affords about twice the window, and decodes a little slower once the window is full. Only matched pairs the CUDA build has flash-attention kernels for are offered: any other type drops attention to the CPU without a word (N100).

idle_minutes.description: How long an on-demand model stays loaded unused.
